title: Granary Ops LLM integration field notes
content:
Call: 2025-01-10 11:00 PST — Granary Ops (regional freight rail) kickoff with Tomás Alvarez and infra team
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood), Riley Thompson (Redwood Sls Eng), Tomás Alvarez (Granary Lead ML), Priya Khatri (Granary SRE), Leah Burns (Redwood Solutions)

High-level ask / context:
- Granary wants a lightweight assistant to help yard operators and dispatchers: 1) manifest summaries, 2) exception triage (delays, missing cargo), 3) natural-language ETA queries.
- Must run in their VPC (private deployment) with at-rest encryption and KMS key ownership.
- Expected QPS: 3–12 requests/sec during peak shift overlaps, burst to 30 for short windows. Token profile: median 120 tokens request, responses 40–160 tokens; occasional long summarizations up to ~800 tokens.
- Hard latency SLO: 95p < 600ms for short queries (<200 tokens); for long summaries acceptable 95p < 3s.

Notable constraints / gotchas discovered:
- Yard connectivity: certain sidings use LTE with high jitter; any client-side retry/backoff will be expensive. Consider local edge cache/proxy if possible.
- Privacy: manifests contain PII (owner contact). Granary insists on audit logs but limited retention (90 days). Need to confirm log redaction policy and whether payloads can be disabled for debug mode.
- Tokenization mismatch: Granary's current prompt framework pre-pends ~300 tokens of system/context for some long workflows (history + policy). Need to validate token budget and consider context-stripping on server side.
- Model selection sensitivity: they want open-models only (license constraints). We'll propose two variants: a Llama-2.1-variant (quantized) for cost and a larger 70B distilled variant for critical summaries. Need to confirm licensing acceptance.
- KV cache usefulness: many requests repeat prefixes (same manifest id, repeated questions). Enable per-customer prefix caching (keyed by manifest-id + route) to cut cost — but confirm cache invalidation rules when manifests are updated in upstream.

Preliminary technical approach (notes):
- Deployment: Redwood Private in their AWS account via VPC mode. Control plane hosted with encrypted control channel; customer KMS.
- Serving config suggestion:
  * Dedicated pool: 1x g5.12x for baseline + autoscale to 2 during peak. Evaluate latency under continuous batching vs single-request mode.
  * Model variants: `gnry-llama-q8` (quantized, cheaper) and `gnry-70b-distill` for high-quality summaries with fallback chain.
  * Routing policy: short queries (<=200 tokens) -> low-latency lane (no batching, strict 10ms scheduling); long summaries -> batch lane (up to 16, 100ms window) with KV prewarm.
  * Cache: prefix cache TTL 5min, explicit invalidation hook from Granary manifest updater service.

Prompting and quality notes:
- Keep prompts template-driven. Example short query template: "User: what is ETA for manifest {{id}}?
System: use latest status, last-seen location, and scheduled transit time."
- For summaries, include a strict output schema (JSON with fields: manifest_id, issues[], summary_text) and use function-style call pattern to ease parser reliability.
- Add guardrails for hallucination: require explicit citation of manifest fields (e.g., "source: manifest.record_42").

Operational / observability requirements from Granary:
- Per-request latency + cost traces for first 60 days.
- Token-level breakdown visible to ops team.
- Alerts if 10%+ of requests hit fallback model in 1h window.
- Audit log export to their S3 bucket daily with KMS encryption.

Open questions to resolve (priority ordered):
1) Licensing approval for proposed open models (Tomás to confirm legal) — ETA next week.
2) Does Granary want raw payloads in logs for 90d? Or redaction by default with opt-in debug? (security)
3) Exact invalidation hook for manifests: webhook or periodic pull? If webhook, provide endpoint spec. (Priya to investigate)
4) SLA negotiation: they ask for 99.9% availability SLA for the Private control-plane channel — we need legal/sales input.
5) On-device edge proxy idea: is there appetite to run a small cache proxy in yard-edge (EC2 t3.medium)? Cost/bandwidth tradeoffs to be assessed.

Action items / next steps (owner + target):
- Tomás: confirm model licensing (open-source acceptability) — due 2025-01-17
- Priya: confirm manifest update workflow and whether webhook can be emitted — due 2025-01-20
- Maya: draft initial serving config (pool + routing + cache rules) and run cost estimate — due 2025-01-16
- Riley: prepare quick demo script that shows short-query latency vs batch summary path; include synthetic jitter network tests — due 2025-01-22
- Leah: add audit log export spec and S3 lifecycle policy template for 90d retention — due 2025-01-18

Experiment ideas (testing hypotheses):
- Hypothesis A: Prefix caching will reduce overall token usage by >= 30% for short queries. Experiment: instrument manifest-based cache keys and compare token counts across 48h on a sample of traffic.
- Hypothesis B: Small-batch window (50–100ms) for summaries yields better cost/latency tradeoff than single-request long-scheduling. Run three A/B variants on synthetic workload.

Misc notes / on-call gotchas (raw):
- If client retries aggressively from LTE yards, we may see double-charges; recommend idempotency keys and server-side dedupe at LB (request-id).
- Consider trimming system prompt in client when client detects manifest length > 1200 tokens to avoid hitting max context. (Add server-side fallback to summarizer).
- Priya flagged desire for offline mode (onboarded caches + queue) — discuss if Redwood can ship a minimal offline-queue component as part of Private bundle.

Meeting cadence suggestion: weekly 30min sync for first 6 weeks; monthly thereafter. Add a standing demo at end of sprint 3.

Notes to self:
- Include a short-playbook on rollback: how to switch default model to smaller quantized variant if latency spikes or cost exceeds threshold.
- Add example webhook spec and JSON schema to next draft.
- Follow up with Legal on model licensing before any infra provisioning.

Last quick sketch (useful logs for debugging):
- Capture these fields per request: request_id, manifest_id, client_location, client_network_type, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, route_taken, cache_hit.

--- end of capture ---

Raw scratch additions (1/25):
- Customer asked for demo scenario: "Delayed inbound, show ETA shift + consignor contact suggestion". Build sample manifest with 12 entries and two exceptions.
- Look into enabling structured outputs as function-calls for manifest-update flow.
